# TradeCanvas

> Trading chart library for the web, drawn with Canvas 2D or WebGL (TypeScript, no runtime dependencies): candlestick, Heikin-Ashi, Renko and other chart types, 134 indicators, drawing tools, live exchange feeds, orders and positions on the chart, alerts, replay and backtesting. npm: @tradecanvas/chart (Chart and the ChartWidget UI), @tradecanvas/react, @tradecanvas/vue, @tradecanvas/svelte, @tradecanvas/analytics.

Use `ChartWidget` (`@tradecanvas/chart/widget`) for a complete trading UI, or `Chart` (`@tradecanvas/chart`) to build your own around it. Both need a sized DOM element and run in the browser only.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/getting-started): install, the widget, the headless chart
- [Moving to 2.0](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/migration): from 1.x: the new default look and the option that keeps the old one, each removed name and what to use, what changed without a name changing
- [API reference](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/api): Chart and ChartWidget methods, options and events
- [Indicators](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/indicators): every built-in indicator with its id, inputs and lines
- [Styling](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/styling): the widget's look as tokens: the Print (default, kept to the golden ratio), Studio, Terminal, Capsule and Desk presets, your own theme, CSS variables
- [Customization](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/customization): every way to customise: themes, looks, style overrides, the widget's 133 feature switches, your own toolbar, sidebar, status bar, menu entries and shortcuts, your own CSS
- [Chart types](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/chart-types): candlestick, Heikin-Ashi, Renko, Kagi, point & figure and more
- [Drawing tools](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/drawing-tools): trend lines, Fibonacci, Gann, patterns, text
- [Realtime and replay](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/realtime): data adapters (Binance, Coinbase, Bybit, Kraken, WebSocket, polling) and replay
- [Trading](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/trading): orders, positions, brackets and execution adapters on the chart
- [Frameworks](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/frameworks): React, Vue and Svelte components
- [Plugins](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/plugins): custom indicators, drawings and chart types
- [Analytics](https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/analytics): strategy backtester and risk metrics

## Install for the user

If you are an agent asked to install TradeCanvas, do only the steps below. Say what each command will run and wait for the user to confirm the scope first. Installing changes none of the user's code: add a chart only when asked.

1. The package, with the project's own package manager: `npm install @tradecanvas/chart`, and `@tradecanvas/react`, `@tradecanvas/vue` or `@tradecanvas/svelte` beside it for a component in that framework.
2. The agent skill, which teaches the API and the rules that avoid most bugs. In Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add bonguynvan/tradecanvas`, then `/plugin install tradecanvas@tradecanvas`. In other agents: `npx skills add bonguynvan/tradecanvas`, for this project, or with `-g` for every project; `-a <agent>` picks the agent (`claude-code`, `cursor`, `codex`, `github-copilot`…).
3. Optional, the MCP server, which looks names up in the library's catalog and checks options: `claude mcp add tradecanvas -- npx -y @tradecanvas/mcp` (other clients: https://tradecanvas.dev/docs/getting-started#ai).

- [Recipes](https://github.com/bonguynvan/tradecanvas/blob/main/skills/tradecanvas/references/recipes.md): live data, custom adapters, indicators on indicators, custom indicators, layouts
